items.author: ScottLEOWarrior
items.context: @ScottLEOWarrior (499.145 seguidores), en inglés: dice que Bitcoin ya va en el 65% de su ciclo de halving actual y que "el próximo capítulo" se acerca. Post de ~1 h con 118 likes, 16 respuestas y 23134 vistas. Ángulo: halving y emisión (subsidio de 3,125 a 1,5625 BTC por bloque, ~450 a ~225 BTC al día, queda 3,125% de los 21M).
items.suggested_text:
Worth keeping in mind what the "next chapter" actually changes on-chain. At the next halving the block subsidy drops from 3.125 to 1.5625 BTC, so new issuance falls from roughly 450 to about 225 BTC a day, and only 3.125% of the 21M cap will still be left to mine.

That makes each halving smaller in absolute terms than the last. The 2012 cut took about 3,600 new coins a day off the market; the next one removes around 225. The supply shock still happens, but it's a shrinking share of what moves price next to demand, leverage and liquidity.

So being 65% through the cycle tells you where the clock is. Whether the halving still sets the rhythm, or demand has quietly taken over that role, is a different question.
